summary: Both sides paint the whole rig one solid colour and step it around the wheel on every beat, but the port's beat detector is frame-count-coupled: it stops firing entirely below ~23 fps (so at the harness default 20 fps the port is a slow silent rainbow fade with zero audio reaction), while the original locks to the 2 Hz beat at every frame rate.
observations: Rig: grid 16x16 / 256 px. Both sides render a SPATIALLY UNIFORM field — a --dump at 0.125/0.275/1.4/2.625 s (fps 40) gave uniqueColors=1 per frame on both sides. There is no spatial structure to compare; the entire pattern is 'what colour is the whole rig, and when does it change'.

Both sides are full-saturation, full-value: meanBrightness min 85 (one channel railed) / max 170 (two channels railed) on every run. No brightness pulsing on either side — the beat drives hue only, not value.

ORIGINAL, fed beat120 at any fps (10/15/20/25/30/40/60 all checked): a hue jump every 0.500 s, i.e. exactly 2.00 jumps/s = one per beat. survey (60 s @10 fps) motion series has non-zero motion on exactly 120 of 600 frames with a gap histogram of {5: 119} — a perfectly regular 5-frame (0.5 s) cadence, 120 events in 60 s.

ORIGINAL hue sequence is a 6-step walk that repeats every 3.0 s (6 beats = one full wheel). Measured plateau RGB at 40 fps: [255,160,0] orange -> [0,255,4] green -> [0,245,255] cyan -> [0,0,255] blue -> [255,0,143] pink -> [255,9,0] red -> repeat. In hue degrees: 38, 121, 182, 240, 326, 2 — i.e. 1/6-turn steps rendered through the Pixel Blaze rainbow hue curve (yellow compressed, magenta stretched).

PORT at the harness default (20 fps), fed beat120: THREE hue jumps in the first 1.3 s and then nothing for the rest of the run. survey (60 s @10 fps) motion is non-zero on 32/600 frames with gaps of ~20 frames (2 s) — those are 8-bit quantisation steps of a smooth ramp, not events. A late-window run (--skip 120 --seconds 20 --fps 20) recorded 0 hue jumps in 20 s while the original did 40.

PORT's steady behaviour at 20 fps is a monotonic hue drift: survey hue went 125 deg at t=2.5 s to 261 deg at t=57.5 s, a constant 2.47 deg/s — visually green -> cyan -> blue -> violet across the whole 60 s (see port-rhythm.png: one smooth vertical gradient, versus the original's ~120 crisp colour bands).

SENSORS-OFF DIAGNOSTIC (--sensors off, 60 s @10 fps) localises it: with dead sensors BOTH sides do the same thing — a slow monotonic hue fade from red (orig reaches 115.5 deg at 60 s, port 148.2 deg). So the shared 'colour fade' base is present and correct on the port; what is missing when fed is the per-beat jump, and the port's fed run is essentially its unfed run plus one startup jump (drift rate identical, 2.47 deg/s fed and unfed).

ROOT CAUSE IS FRAME-RATE COUPLING, measured directly. Port beat-jump rate vs fps (30 s windows, fed): 10 fps 0.20/s, 15 fps 0.07/s, 20 fps 0.50/s (all in the first second), 21 fps 0.15/s, 22 fps 0.15/s, 23 fps 1.05/s, 24 fps 2.00/s, 25 fps 2.03/s, 30 fps 2.03/s, 40 fps 2.03/s, 60 fps 2.00/s. The original posts 2.00/s at every one of those rates. The cutover at 23-24 fps against a 0.5 s beat implies the port's beat history spans a fixed ~12 RENDER FRAMES rather than a fixed time window.

WHEN THE PORT DOES RUN (fps >= 24) its rhythm matches the original exactly: jumps at 0.575, 1.075, 1.575, 2.075, 2.575, 3.075 s ... i.e. every 0.500 s, and the same 6-step / 3.0 s repeating hue cycle. The remaining differences at 40 fps are colour placement and phase, below.

COLOUR-STOP DIFFERENCE (both at 40 fps, matched cadence). Original's six plateau colours: [255,160,0] orange, [0,255,4] green, [0,245,255] cyan, [0,0,255] blue, [255,0,143] pink, [255,9,0] red. Port's six: [0,255,1] green, [0,252,255] cyan, [3,0,255] blue, [175,0,255] purple, [255,2,0] red, [251,255,0] yellow. Same wheel, same direction, same 1/6-turn step, but the port's stops sit on a near-linear hue ramp (0/60/120/180/240/281 deg) instead of the original's PB rainbow ramp (2/38/121/182/240/326 deg). Net visible effect: where the original shows ORANGE and PINK, the port shows YELLOW and PURPLE; the other four stops agree within a couple of degrees.

PHASE OFFSET: the port fires an extra jump in the first 0.15 s (jumps at 0.050 s and 0.150 s vs the original's single 0.100 s), so from then on the port's colour cycle runs one step (1/6 turn) ahead of the original's for the rest of the run.

IDLE FADE RATE: with sensors off, the port fades faster than the original at every FadeSpeed. Hue travelled in 60 s at FadeSpeed 0 / 0.5 / 1 — orig 19.8 / 115.5 / 210.8 deg, port 42.8 / 148.0 / 256.7 deg. Converted to wheel fractions that is orig 0.089 / 0.324 / 0.586 turns per minute vs port 0.178 / 0.410 / 0.701 — same slope, roughly a constant +0.10 turns/min offset, so the port is 2.0x too fast at FadeSpeed 0 and ~1.2x too fast at FadeSpeed 1. The fade itself is time-based (not frame-coupled) on both sides: orig 115.5 deg @10 fps vs 101.6 deg @40 fps, port 148.2 vs 144.9.

CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH: the original exposes sliderBeatSensitivity, showNumberBeatSensitivity, sliderFadeSpeed, showNumberFadeSpeed. The port exposes sliderBeatSensitivity, showNumberBeatBuffer, sliderFadeSpeed, showNumberFadeSpeed. The second display readout is renamed and shows a different quantity (BeatBuffer vs BeatSensitivity). Both sliders match by name and kind.

Seed has no effect on either side (seed 1234 at 40 fps reproduced seed 1 byte-for-byte in the stats series) — the pattern is fully driven by the deterministic sensor feed, so there is no stochastic character to compare.

No mode/regime structure on either side: the survey rhythm images show one uniform texture for the whole 60 s (orig: even 0.5 s bands throughout; port: one continuous gradient), and the late window at t=120-140 s behaves exactly like t=0-20 s for both. brightnessTrend 'steady' on both sides in every run.

dials.name: sliderBeatSensitivity
dials.origEffect: No observable effect. Swept 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1 over 30 s windows at 10 fps (60 beat events each) and again at 0 / 0.5 / 1 at 40 fps: every value produced exactly 60 hue jumps in 30 s and the identical hue sequence (RGB at t=1.4 s was [0,241,255] at all values). Probe also reported maxDelta 0.00 over a 12 s window. Recorded as 'dial effect unverifiable from output' under the beat120 feed — the synthetic beat is presumably above threshold at every setting.
dials.portEffect: Live and strong (probe maxDelta 209.2), and it gates beat detection. At 20 fps default the setting only changes how many of the handful of start-up jumps survive: 4 / 4 / 3 / 2 / 0 jumps at 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1 (all inside the first 1.3 s; nothing afterwards at any value). At 40 fps, where the port's detector works, 0 and 0.5 both give the full 2.03 jumps/s but 1 kills beat response completely (0 jumps in 30 s, port reverts to pure fade). So on the port the slider is a hard threshold that can switch the pattern's whole reason for existing off.

dials.name: sliderFadeSpeed
dials.origEffect: Live, monotonic: higher = faster idle hue drift. Isolated with --sensors off over 60 s, hue travelled 19.8 / 115.5 / 210.8 deg at 0 / 0.5 / 1 (0.089 / 0.324 / 0.586 wheel-turns per minute), roughly linear with a small non-zero floor. Under the beat120 feed its effect is invisible next to the beat jumps (probe maxDelta 1.19, net hue travel 3600 deg/30 s regardless of setting).
dials.portEffect: Live, monotonic, same direction: 42.8 / 148.0 / 256.7 deg per 60 s at 0 / 0.5 / 1 with sensors off (0.178 / 0.410 / 0.701 turns/min). Same slope as the original but shifted up by ~0.10 turns/min, so the port fades 2.0x too fast at FadeSpeed 0 and ~1.2x too fast at FadeSpeed 1. Under the fed run at 20 fps this drift is the only thing happening at all.

feedback: PRIMARY BUG — the port's beat detector measures its history in RENDER FRAMES, not in seconds. Measured cutover: it produces the correct 2.00 beat-jumps/s at 24 fps and above, degrades at 23 fps (1.05/s), and produces essentially nothing at 22 fps and below (0.07-0.50/s, and all of those jumps are inside the first ~1.3 s). Against a 0.5 s beat interval, a 24 fps cutover means the running buffer/average spans about 12 frames. Rebase whatever window, decay or averaging the beat detector uses onto elapsed time (accumulate the frame delta) so the detector's memory covers a fixed number of SECONDS. Target: identical 2.00 jumps/s at 10, 15, 20, 25, 40 and 60 fps, matching the original which is already invariant across all of those.

Verify the fix at the harness default 20 fps specifically: a passing run shows non-zero motion on exactly every 10th frame (0.5 s cadence) and 12 hue jumps in the 6 s baseline window, versus the current 3 jumps that all land before t=1.3 s.

COLOUR STOPS — at matched cadence (40 fps) the port steps the same 1/6-turn per beat but renders those stops on a linear hue ramp instead of the Pixel Blaze rainbow ramp. Two of the six stops are visibly wrong: at step 1 the original shows ORANGE [255,160,0] where the port shows YELLOW [251,255,0], and at step 5 the original shows PINK [255,0,143] where the port shows PURPLE [175,0,255]. The other four (red [255,9,0], green [0,255,4], cyan [0,245,255], blue [0,0,255]) already agree. Route the port's colour through the same hue curve the engine's hsv() uses rather than a hand-rolled linear hue-to-RGB conversion.

PHASE — the port emits an extra beat jump during the first 0.15 s (jumps at 0.050 s and 0.150 s where the original has one at 0.100 s), which leaves the port's colour cycle permanently one step ahead. Suppress the spurious first-frame trigger: the detector should not fire until its history window has actually been filled.

IDLE FADE RATE — the port's slow fade is uniformly too fast: at FadeSpeed 0 it drifts 0.178 wheel-turns/min against the original's 0.089 (2.0x), and at FadeSpeed 1 it drifts 0.701 against 0.586 (1.20x). The slope across the slider is right; the floor/offset is roughly doubled. Reduce the constant term of the fade rate so FadeSpeed 0 gives ~0.09 turns/min and FadeSpeed 1 gives ~0.59 turns/min (measure with --sensors off, 60 s, since the beat jumps swamp this under the fed run).

BEAT SENSITIVITY — on the original this slider makes no difference at all across 0..1 under the synthetic beat (60 jumps in 30 s at every value, identical colours). On the port, setting it to 1 disables beat response entirely even at 40 fps. Whatever threshold the port derives from the slider is far too aggressive at the top of its range; it should stay reactive to a strong beat across the whole slider range, as the original does.

CONTROL SURFACE — the original's second display control is named showNumberBeatSensitivity (echoing the slider); the port exposes showNumberBeatBuffer instead. Rename it and show the same quantity so the UI matches the original's.

Nothing spatial needs work: both sides already paint a single uniform full-saturation colour across the whole rig, with matching brightness envelope (mean 85 on a primary, 170 on a secondary), and the port's sensors-off fallback behaviour already matches the original's.
